Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, MoS for Power and New & Renewable Energy, leads Indian delegation to Singapore International Energy Week 2026
articles.full_content:
Holds bilateral meetings with Singapore, Bhutan, IRENA and IEA on the sidelines
The Union Minister of State for Power and New & Renewable Energy, Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, led the Indian delegation to the Singapore International Energy Week (SIEW) 2026, held at the Marina Bay Sands Expo and Convention Centre, Singapore, from 26th to 28th October 2026.
SIEW 2026 coincided with the 25th year of Singapore's Energy Market Authority. The Summit was expanded into a two-day event this year and featured the Singapore-IEA Forum, the Singapore-IRENA Forum, and the IAEA at SIEW. Shri Naik participated and delivered a keynote on Day 1 and the Opening Remarks for the 2nd day of the event.
Addressing sessions on the first two days of the event, Shri Naik said India’s installed electricity capacity stood at 558.9 GW as of 30 September 2026, of which about 308 GW, or 55 per cent, came from non-fossil sources. He noted that India achieved 50 per cent non-fossil installed capacity in June 2025, five years ahead of its 2030 NDC target, and is now working towards 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030. Highlighting progress under the flagship schemes, he said that around 53 lakh rooftop solar systems had been installed under PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, benefiting about 63 lakh households. Under PM-KUSUM, nearly 12 lakh standalone solar pumps have been installed, and more than 17 lakh grid-connected agricultural pumps have been solarised, adding about 16.7 GW of decentralised renewable energy capacity and benefiting around 30 lakh farmers.
Shri Naik also held bilateral meetings with the following countries/organisations on the sidelines of SIEW 2026:
Singapore : Shri Naik met Ms Gan Siow Huang, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Energy and Trade and Industry, Republic of Singapore. The two sides discussed energy cooperation under the India-Singapore Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, including the proposed cross-border electricity interconnection between the two countries. Shri Naik invited long-term Singaporean investment in transmission, pumped storage, battery storage and renewable energy in India. Cooperation in green hydrogen and ammonia, energy efficiency, and partnerships between Indian power equipment manufacturers and Singapore's utilities was also discussed.
Bhutan : Shri Naik met H.E. Lyonpo Sonam Tashi, Minister for Energy and Natural Resources, Royal Government of Bhutan, and congratulated him on assuming office. The two Ministers reviewed progress on the 1200 MW Punatsangchhu-I Hydroelectric Project, where dam works have progressed steadily since concreting resumed in April 2026, and noted the satisfactory operations of the 1020 MW Punatsangchhu-II project. They also discussed the other projects that are under discussion in partnership with Indian entities, along with the cross-border transmission planning up to 2040.
IRENA : Shri Naik met Mr Francesco La Camera, Director-General, International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA). He appreciated IR

SIEW 2026 coincided with the 25th year of Singapore's Energy Market Authority. The Summit was expanded into a two-day event this year and featured the Singapore-IEA Forum, the Singapore-IRENA Forum, and the IAEA at SIEW.

Green Hydrogen
articles.full_content:
Emerging Pillar of India’s Clean Energy Transition
Green hydrogen is emerging as a pillar of India’s clean energy transition. It is produced by splitting water using renewable electricity. It can help reduce emissions in sectors such as fertiliser production, petroleum refining, iron and steel manufacturing, heavy-duty road transport and shipping . The National Green Hydrogen Mission (NGHM) supports domestic manufacturing, production, assured demand and credible certification. From green ammonia auctions to India’s first hydrogen train, early projects point to a promising path.
Why Green Hydrogen
Hydrogen is an energy carrier that stores energy and delivers it for varied uses. In a fuel cell, it reacts with oxygen to produce electricity, leaving only water and heat as by-products, and no polluting compounds or greenhouse gases. Although pure hydrogen is not found in large quantities in nature, it can be extracted from compounds such as water or natural gas. Its environmental impact therefore depends on how it is made. Conventional methods rely on fossil fuels and release carbon emissions.
Production using renewable electricity from solar and wind power can cut this footprint substantially. Hydrogen made by splitting water using renewable power is called green hydrogen . Unlike fossil-based routes, this process emits far less carbon. India’s abundant solar and wind resources make domestic production feasible. This diversifies the country’s energy sources and strengthens energy security. It also supports India’s goal of net-zero emissions by 2070.
Green hydrogen matters most in sectors where cutting emissions is difficult. Reasons include high-temperature heat needs, chemical processes and few alternatives to fossil fuels. These hard-to-abate sectors include fertiliser, petroleum refining, iron and steel, heavy-duty road transport and shipping. Fertiliser and refining plants already use hydrogen, so green hydrogen can replace the fossil-based supply. It can also support lower-emission steelmaking, selected transport uses and energy storage. It is especially useful where direct electrification is difficult or less practical.
For India, wider adoption could reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels. It would also lessen exposure to global fuel price swings. The sector could open opportunities in manufacturing, draw investment, create jobs and expand exports. Building capabilities across the value chain would strengthen domestic supply chains and spur industrial innovation. Green hydrogen can thus support self-reliance, sustainable industrial growth and a low-carbon future.
What Makes Hydrogen “Green”
Hydrogen releases no carbon dioxide when used, so its climate impact depends on how it is produced. In August 2023, the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) notified India’s Green Hydrogen Standard. Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Interacts with Export Promotion Councils, Calls for Greater Export Competitiveness and Market Diversification
articles.full_content:
Shri Piyush Goyal Reviews Export Scenario with Export Promotion Councils, Emphasises Market Access and Global Competitiveness Shri Goyal Highlights Government Measures to Facilitate Exports and Address Challenges Faced by Exporters
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal, interacted with representatives of Export Promotion Councils (EPCs) in New Delhi today to review the prevailing export scenario, discuss emerging opportunities and challenges in international trade, and deliberate on measures to further strengthen India’s export competitiveness.
During the interaction, Shri Goyal highlighted the evolving global trade environment, characterised by geopolitical uncertainties, changes in tariff structures, supply chain realignments and emerging regulatory requirements in major international markets. He noted that while these developments pose challenges for exporters, they also present opportunities for India to strengthen its position as a reliable and competitive global trading partner.
Shri Goyal emphasised the need for Indian industry to remain agile and responsive to the changing international business environment. He encouraged exporters to focus on improving product quality, innovation, cost competitiveness, reliability of supply and compliance with international standards to enhance India’s participation in global value chains.
Referring to his recent international engagements, including his visits to Germany and the Netherlands, Shri Goyal highlighted the growing interest in India as a manufacturing, sourcing and investment destination. He stressed the importance of translating these engagements into tangible business outcomes through sustained interaction between Indian industry and overseas businesses. He encouraged EPCs to engage proactively with their international counterparts, identify potential buyers and facilitate business partnerships in established and emerging markets.
The Minister also highlighted the importance of effectively leveraging the opportunities arising from India's expanding network of Free trade agreements and economic partnerships. He emphasised that preferential market access under Free Trade Agreements must translate into increased exports, greater market penetration and wider participation of Indian enterprises in international trade. EPCs were encouraged to undertake sector-specific assessments of export opportunities in partner countries and strengthen awareness among exporters regarding applicable trade preferences, standards and market requirements.
Shri Goyal also emphasised the need for a focused approach towards product and market diversification in response to changing global demand and emerging supply chain opportunities. He encouraged EPCs to identify products with untapped export potential, explore new destinations and develop market-specific strategies. He highlighted the importance of consolidating India’s competitive advantages in established sectors while building capabilities

articles.full_content:
The three-day Regional Training Workshop on Base Year Revision of the State Level Index of Industrial Production (IIP) commenced at Hotel Dimora International, Thiruvananthapuram, on 28 October 2026. The workshop was organized by Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Government of India, in collaboration with Department of Economics & Statistics (DES), Government of Keralam. The workshop will continue until 30 October 2026.
Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics), MoSPI, formally inaugurating the workshop.
The programme began with lamp lighting by the dignitaries. Inaugural session of the three days workshop was graced by the distinguished dignitaries, including the Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics), MoSPI, Shri Gokul G. R., IAS, Special Secretary, Planning & Economic Affairs Department, Government of Keralam, Shri Deepak Dhanawat, Director, MoSPI, Ms. Shailamma K, Director, Directorate of Economics & Statistics, Keralam and by Shri V. K.
Sreejan, Additional Director, Directorate of Economics & Statistics, Keralam. The Workshop was attended by approximately 60 participants from 16 States/UTs.
Ms. Shailamma K, Director, Directorate of Economics & Statistics, Keralam, welcomed the dignitaries and participants, acknowledged the support of MoSPI and organising the regional training programme, and highlighted the importance of strengthening the technical capacity of State statistical offices for the effective implementation of the IIP base-year revision exercise.
Shri Deepak Dhanawat, Director, MoSPI, outlined the objectives and background of the workshop. He has highlighted on the importance of State IIP in tracking the industrial performance if State. He stressed that States should compile the same methodology as the All India IIP.
Shri Gokul G. R., IAS, Special Secretary, Planning & Economic Affairs Department, Government of Keralam, presided over the inaugural session. In his presidential address, Shri Gokul G. R., IAS, highlighted the growing public importance of reliable official statistics in a context where economic information is widely discussed through social media and where individual participation in financial and retail investment has increased. He observed that timely, credible and methodologically sound statistics are essential for informed public discussion and evidence-based policy decisions. He stressed that the item basket used for compiling the IIP should reflect the current structure of industry and changes in production patterns. He also emphasised the need to strengthen the quality of primary data collection, minimise measurement errors and ensure that the information furnished by reporting units accurately represents industrial activity.

Ministry of New and Renewable Energy Steps Up E-Waste Management under Special Campaign 6
articles.full_content:
Identifies 5,337 Obsolete E-Waste Items for Disposal
The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) is undertaking focused efforts for the effective collection, segregation and disposal of electronic waste (e-waste). With the objective of institutionalising Swachhata and promoting efficient resource management, the activity is being undertaken as part of Special Campaign 6 for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM 6).
Under the campaign, 5,337 obsolete and e-waste items have been identified for disposal. The obsolete/ e-waste items are being disposed of through auction, thereby generating revenue and facilitating the optimal utilisation of available space. The disposal process has generated revenue amounting to ₹11,40,220/- so far and resulted in the clearance of approximately 600 sq. ft. of space.
The campaign places special emphasis on the systematic identification, segregation and responsible disposal of obsolete electronic items, while ensuring better utilisation of office space and improved workplace organisation.
Through these sustained efforts, MNRE reaffirms its commitment to Swachhata, environmentally responsible waste management and efficient administrative practices under Special Campaign 6.

· Australia, Denmark, European Union, France, Germany, Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, United Kingdom to Participate as Country Partners
· Thirteen States and Union Territories will participate in the Summit, including Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Delhi, Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal, showcasing their renewable energy potential, investment opportunities and manufacturing capabilities.
. National and Global Exhibitors to Showcase Renewable Energy Technologies; National Hackathon, Renewable Energy Quiz and REGen Pavilion Among Key Attractions
The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Government of India, is organising the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo (BRESE) 2026 from 2–5 November 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. The Hon'ble Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, will inaugurate the Summit on 2 nd November 2026.
Shri Santosh Sarangi, Secretary, Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, Government of India, while addressing media persons here today said, “India's clean energy transition is entering a decisive phase. With 308 GW of installed non-fossil fuel capacity, we are firmly on course to reach our 500 GW target by 2030. Realising this ambition will require approximately USD 220 billion in investment between 2027 and 2030, alongside accelerated deployment of energy storage, stronger transmission networks and expanded domestic manufacturing capabilities. The Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026 will provide a vital platform to connect global capital, technology and industry expertise with India's growing clean energy opportunities, translating investment potential into projects, partnerships and progress.”
The four-day event, themed 'Invest. Innovate. Inspire.', is expected to bring together participants from over 130 countries, including ministers, policymakers, industry leaders, investors, financial institutions, manufacturers, innovators, researchers and representatives of multilateral organisations. The Summit will be organised alongside the 9th Session of the International Solar Alliance (ISA) Assembly and the 4th International Conference on Green Hydrogen (ICGH). The three events will provide a common platform for discussions on renewable energy investment, international cooperation, emerging technologies and clean energy deployment.
Australia, Denmark, the European Union, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, and the United Kingdom will participate as country partners. Delegations from several other countries are also expected to attend the Summit to explore cooperation opportunities in renewable energy financing, green hydrogen, energy storage, clean energy manufacturing, and technology development.

MCL Hosts Street Plays To Promote E-Waste Management Under Special Campaign 6
articles.full_content:
Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL) a subsidiary of Coal India Limited under the Ministry of Coal, organised a nukkad natak (street play) at its headquarters under Special Campaign 6 to spread awareness about e-waste management, responsible disposal of electronic waste and allied environmental issues.
GM (Civil/Wel-TA & CSR), Heads of Departments, officers and staff attended the programme. Smt. Rekha Pandey, Director (HR), encouraged employees to contribute towards a cleaner work environment and a sustainable future.
The street play highlighted the importance of environmentally responsible practices for the collection, segregation and scientific disposal of electronic waste. Through an interactive presentation, the programme emphasised the need to reduce, reuse and recycle electronic items and ensure that discarded electrical and electronic equipment is channelled through authorised e-waste collection and recycling systems.
The initiative aligns with the theme of Special Campaign 6, being observed from October 2 to October 31, 2026, with a focus on e-waste management. The programme also reinforced the broader objectives of Special Campaign 6, including promoting environmental responsibility, encouraging sustainable workplace practices and strengthening collective participation in cleanliness and waste-management initiatives.
Through such awareness activities, MCL continues to encourage its employees to adopt responsible waste-management practices and contribute towards the vision of a cleaner environment and a greener tomorrow.

DGFT to Organise Karnataka State Workshop on Leveraging Free Trade Agreements to Boost FTA Utilisation
articles.full_content:
The Office of the Additional Director General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Bengaluru, in collaboration with the Government of Karnataka and the Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO), is organising a state-level workshop on leveraging Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) on 30 October 2026 at The Lalit Ashok, Bengaluru. The workshop aims to raise awareness and facilitate the effective utilisation of India’s FTAs, with a focus on enhancing market access and strengthening Karnataka’s export competitiveness.
Shri M. B. Patil, Hon’ble Minister for Large and Medium Industries, Government of Karnataka, is expected to inaugurate the event and address the exporters. Senior officials from the Government of Karnataka and the Government of India are also expected to attend the event, address the participants, and interact with exporters.
The workshop is expected to bring together nearly 200 participants, including leading exporters from the State, officials from the District Industries Centres (DICs) of the Government of Karnataka, representatives of Export Promotion Councils (EPCs), and other stakeholders from the trade and industry ecosystem.
The technical sessions will include a presentation on FTA opportunities in the services sector by Dr. Abhay Sinha, Director General, Services Export Promotion Council. Dr. Tamanna Chaturvedi, Trade Advisor, India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO), will deliver a session on recently signed FTAs, emerging opportunities for Karnataka, and suggested interventions to enhance the State’s export potential.
A dedicated sectoral discussion will focus on identifying export opportunities and recommending practical interventions across four key sectors: agriculture, dairy, marine products and food processing; textiles, apparel and made-ups; engineering, electronics and semiconductors; and services.
Through this outreach initiative, DGFT seeks to strengthen stakeholder awareness, facilitate the effective utilisation of India’s FTAs, and promote greater access to international markets. The programme is expected to support the identification of sector-specific opportunities and practical interventions to enhance Karnataka’s export growth, particularly by leveraging emerging opportunities arising from recently signed FTAs.
articles.summary: The Office of the Additional Director General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Bengaluru, in collaboration with the Government of Karnataka and the Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO), is organising a state-level workshop on leveraging Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) on 30 October 2026 at The Lalit Ashok, Bengaluru. The workshop aims to raise awareness and facilitate the effective utilisation of India’s FTAs, with a focus on enhancing market access and strengthening Karnataka’s export competitiveness. Patil, Hon’ble Minister for Large and Medium Industries, Government of Karnataka, is expected to inaugurate the event and address the exporters.

articles.full_content:
Minimum Turnover criterion for Part 2 of the Scheme reduced to ₹100 Crore
Ministry of Textiles is set to reopen the application portal for the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Textiles for accepting new applications under Round 4 of the Scheme from 1st November 2026 till 31st December 2026 to promote the manufacturing of Man-Made Fibre (MMF) Apparel, MMF Fabrics and Technical Textiles, enhance domestic manufacturing capabilities, attract investment, generate employment and strengthen India's position in global textile value chains.
To facilitate wider participation under the Scheme, the following key modifications have also been made in the Scheme:
1. Reduction in Minimum Turnover Criterion: The minimum turnover requirement has been reduced from ₹200 crore to ₹100 crore under Part 2 category of the scheme, enabling greater participation by MSMEs and mid-sized manufacturing units.
2. Extension of Scheme Tenure: The scheme tenure has been extended up to Financial Year 2033–34 exclusively for applicants approved under Round 4. The extended tenure is intended to provide these applicants with a longer investment and operational horizon for establishing and scaling up their manufacturing capacities.
3. Migration of Existing Participant Companies of the Scheme to Round 4 : All existing participant companies of Round 1, 2 & 3, in any part of the Scheme, that have not claimed or received any incentive so far, are also eligible to migrate under Round 4, subject to withdrawal of their existing applications under Round 1, 2 and 3, as applicable.
The online application portal https://pli.texmin.gov.in will remain open from 1st November 2026 till 31st December 2026 . Eligible companies are encouraged to submit their applications within the stipulated period in accordance with the applicable scheme guidelines.

The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, has driven a sustained shift from a permission-based to a trust-based regulatory framework. Reforms across the startup ecosystem, compliance reduction, sectoral regulation, foreign direct investment and single-window clearances have reduced the regulatory burden on businesses and delivered measurable outcomes in business entry, employment, investment and digital service delivery.
DPIIT has recognised 2,50,046 startups, reporting over 25.42 lakh jobs across 770+ districts and 56 industries. Of these startups, 52% are from non-metro cities and 48% have at least one woman director. Annual recognitions increased from 34,200 in FY 2023-24 to 36,440 in FY 2024-25.
Under the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme, ₹775.67 crore has been approved for 4,194 startups across 32 States/UTs through 244 incubators, including 2,147 women-led startups and 2,356 startups from Tier-II and Tier-III cities. Under the Fund of Funds for Startups, SIDBI has committed ₹12,623 crore to 166 Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), which have invested ₹28,254 crore in 1,475 startups.
The Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups has guaranteed 532 loans worth ₹1,662.71 crore to startups employing 41,637 people. The guarantee cover per borrower has been doubled from ₹10 crore to ₹20 crore, while the annual fee has been reduced to 1% for 27 Champion Sectors.
A total of 63 regulatory reforms have been enabled, including the abolition of angel tax, harmonisation of long-term capital gains taxation for listed and unlisted shares, and permission for insurance companies, EPFO, superannuation funds and gratuity funds to invest in AIFs. In addition, 104 new incubators have been established across 17 States/UTs, while the TEJAS initiative covers 132 districts in 27 States/UTs.

The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, has launched the 6th Edition of the National Startup Awards (NSA 6.0) under the Startup India initiative to recognise innovation and entrepreneurship and strengthen India’s startup ecosystem.
The year 2026 marks the completion of ten years of the Startup India initiative, launched in January 2016 to build a strong, inclusive and innovation-driven entrepreneurial ecosystem in the country. Since its inception in 2019, the National Startup Awards have emerged as a flagship initiative under Startup India, providing a national platform to recognise entrepreneurial excellence and showcase innovative solutions addressing critical challenges across sectors.
The National Startup Awards recognise startups demonstrating outstanding performance in innovation, scalability, sustainability and socio-economic impact. Building upon the success of the previous five editions, NSA 6.0 seeks to strengthen India’s startup ecosystem by encouraging innovation-led entrepreneurship, fostering inclusive participation and promoting globally competitive startups.
NSA 6.0 will recognise innovation, entrepreneurship and excellence across 20 sectoral categories and three special award categories, reflecting India’s evolving startup ecosystem, emerging technologies and national development priorities. Workshop on Base Revision of State -level Index of Industrial Production during 28–30 October 2026 at Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) is convening a three Days Workshop on Base Revision of State-level Index of Industrial Production (IIP), at Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam in collaboration with Department of Economics and Statistics (DES), Keralam during 28–30 October 2026.
The IIP is a key indicator of industrial performance, tracking changes in performance of industrial sector in economy. It is widely used by policymakers, economists, businesses and investors to assess trends in industrial activity and support informed decision-making. The index also serves as an important input in estimating overall economic growth.
MoSPI has updated the base year of the All-India IIP from 2011-12 to 2022-23. The base year is the reference year against which changes in production in later years are measured. A more recent base year helps the index reflect what India’s industries actually produce at present. The revised series incorporates several methodological improvements, including revision of the item basket and weights, updating of the factory panel, expansion of coverage to include activities such as Gas Supply, Water Supply, Sewerage and Waste Management and provision for factory substitution.
The State DES are responsible for compiling and disseminating the State-level IIP. As the nodal Ministry at the national level, the MoSPI provides technical guidance to States and Union Territories (UTs) to promote methodological uniformity and improve the quality and comparability of industrial statistics.
The three-day workshop will familiarise participating States and UTs with the proposed changes in the structure and methods of the revised IIP and help them finalise the list of items to be tracked and the factories that will report data. It will also provide a platform for discussions and feedback on the revisions to National Industrial Classification-2025 and National Product Classification.
Around 60 officials from MoSPI and the DESs of various States and UTs are expected to take part. Through this workshop, MoSPI aims to strengthen the quality, consistency and comparability of industrial statistics across the country.

India’s Genetic Diversity Could Make It a Global Destination for Gene Research: Dr. Jitendra Singh
articles.full_content:
Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh addresses Session on System and Synthetic Biology at ESTIC 2026, stressing India’s potential in gene research and biotechnology India’s diverse genetic and phenotypic profile offers significant opportunities for scientific research and healthcare innovation Focus on developing domestic gene-synthesis capabilities and strengthening India’s biotechnology ecosystem: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, has said that India’s rich genetic diversity holds significant potential to make the country an important global resource for gene research, with other nations looking towards India for its unique genetic resources in the coming years.
Addressing a session on System and Synthetic Biology at the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, Dr. Jitendra Singh emphasised the need to build domestic capabilities in emerging areas of biotechnology and translate India’s scientific strengths into research opportunities and practical applications.
The Minister said India’s remarkable genetic and phenotypic diversity provides a valuable foundation for research, particularly in understanding variations in disease patterns and exploring new possibilities in healthcare. He expressed confidence that as India develops and scales up its research capabilities, the country can emerge as an important source of genetic resources for the global scientific community.
Dr. Jitendra Singh also stressed the importance of strengthening indigenous technological capabilities in gene synthesis. Dependence on overseas suppliers for specialised research requirements can create challenges for Indian scientists in terms of time, access and research continuity. Building domestic capabilities in this area would help researchers pursue their work more efficiently and strengthen the country’s biotechnology ecosystem.
The Minister said India has considerable scientific talent and that the government has accorded high priority to research and innovation. He emphasised the need to strengthen the support systems required to take research forward, including greater industry participation and funding for promising scientific work.
Dr. Jitendra Singh also spoke about the growing convergence of disciplines and the need to bring together biology, engineering, mathematics and other areas of expertise. Such interdisciplinary collaboration is becoming increasingly important as scientific research moves towards more complex applications and new technology pathways.

Artisans and craftspeople under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme of the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises participated at the two-day Cultural Bazar organised during the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum at the Parliament House Complex, New Delhi, on 26–27 October 2026.
The Cultural Bazar provided a platform to showcase India’s rich cultural heritage, traditional crafts, artisan-made products and indigenous skills to national and international delegates attending the BRICS Parliamentary Forum. The participation highlighted the diversity of India’s traditional craftsmanship and the contribution of artisan communities to preserving the country’s cultural legacy. BRICS delegates also appreciated the products made by Vishwakarmas.

Selected artisans also conducted live demonstrations of traditional craft-making techniques, offering visitors an opportunity to witness the skills and craftsmanship involved in creating these products.
